titre: Analyst proves "Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed" using the power of math
chapo: The Fool update has been a huge boost for Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder

The Fool update has been a huge boost for Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder I didn't need anybody to tell me that "Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed" – of course I know him, he's me – but new data from market analysis head Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics certainly puts the depth of the community's devotion into perspective. In a report, Elliott estimates that developer Mega Crit has sold 7.9 million copies of Slay the Spire 2 through Steam, where it's still in early access. Owner estimations on SteamDB support this figure, ranging from 6.8 million to 7.8 million. But that's not the impressive number. We already knew that Slay the Spire 2 is a massive success and handily the biggest game of its kind. Here's a truly enviable figure: "The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9M folks have played for over 100 hours," Elliott finds. "That means 24% of the 7.8M player base have put over 100 hours in. About 100K folks have bought Slay the Spire 2 on Steam but haven’t booted up yet, hence the difference between copies and players." Look under some rocks around Steam stats, PlayStation trophies, or Xbox achievements and you may be horrified to learn that a lot of people don't finish or play very much of the games they buy. A game's average completion time is reliably an entire zip code away from its median playtime. So it's in stats like this that we truly see how Slay the Spire 2 is not only popular, but sticky. Behold, the quantified power of one more run. "Slay the Spire II has never had fewer than 2.5M active players in a month since launching back in March, and this month is already up on October, thanks to a chunky update that adds a new character," Elliott notes. Additionally, "about 65K absolute nutters (nearly 1% of the player base) have played Slay the Spire II for over 500 hours (!!!)." That is, indeed, an alarmingly large population of absolute nutters. Most games would kill for 1%. Don't tell my stack of unplayed games, but I'm approaching 300 hours of sequel spire slaying myself, now focusing on Ascension 10 with the new Fool character and having a blast. titre: Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"
chapo: One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March. Read more
extrait: One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March. That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio. Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on. We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue. It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said. Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March. Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active users to reach its highest daily player count in six months. "Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours." Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.
